To whom it may concern,  

I’ve worked alongside Kenji Mori on cross-team security initiatives at a FAANG company, where he contributed to projects involving identity systems and infrastructure protection. While our collaboration was occasional, his work consistently intersected with our goals, particularly in securing sensitive data workflows.  

Kenji’s strength lies in his ability to balance technical rigor with pragmatic problem-solving. He’s deeply involved in designing IAM systems that align with regulatory requirements, and his approach to access control has reduced unauthorized access risks by over 40% in the platforms he owns. His recent work refining session management for a HIPAA-compliant API suite exemplifies this—by implementing token-based revocation, he minimized exposure during credential compromises without complicating user flows.  

Beyond technical expertise, Kenji’s dedication to security hygiene is notable. He leads penetration testing efforts with a focus on scenario-driven testing, often identifying overlooked attack vectors in cloud-native applications. His mentorship has helped junior engineers adopt a mindset of proactive defense, such as embedding security checks into CI/CD pipelines.  

Kenji’s reliability and curiosity make him a trusted collaborator. He approaches challenges with a methodical, no-nonsense attitude that’s hard to replicate. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss his contributions further.  

Sincerely,  
[Recommender’s Name]
